title: Combining antigen-specific vaccination with radiopharmaceutical therapy (RPT) to enhance anti-tumor immunity and efficacy
text:
Novel therapeutic approaches to the treatment of advanced prostate cancer are needed due to the limited
efficacy of current treatments. Combining tumor-specific vaccination to activate CD8+ T cells and
radiopharmaceutical therapy to deplete tumor-infiltrating suppressive populations may be a promising approach
to enhance anti-tumor immunity and efficacy. This proposal aims to target immunoresistance mechanisms of
prostate cancer using radiopharmaceutical therapy, which will be critical for determining the selection and timing
with immunotherapies, potentially prolonging the lives of patients.

title: Decision Processes in Late-Life Suicide
text:
In this competitive renewal examining risk factors of late-life suicide attempts (which are common and highly
lethal), we extend and enrich our prospective longitudinal study by continuing annual clinical and cognitive
assessments. As a novel addition, we will integrate long-term (months or years) and short-term (daily)
measures of suicide risk factors, including suicidal ideation, affect, social functioning, cognition, and sleep
health to capture the multi-dimensional and dynamic nature of suicide risk.

title: Optical Precision Targeting for Informed Cancer biopsy (OPTIC)
text:
LEADOPTIK is developing the LIA System, a novel biopsy needle with integrated OCT that enables real-time,
high-resolution visualization of lung tissue during needle advancement, addressing the longstanding challenge
of blind biopsies in PPL diagnosis. Current technologies like r-EBUS suffer from low diagnostic yield due to the
need to remove imaging probes prior to sampling, while alternatives like CT-guided transthoracic biopsy carry
high complication rates and robotic platforms fail to resolve “last inch” targeting. This Direct-to-Phase II project
will initiate a first-in-human clinical trial to demonstrate the LIA System’s accuracy, safety, and usability, with the
ultimate goal of transforming lung cancer diagnosis through precise, image-guided tissue acquisition.

title: Leveraging access to parasite natural diversity to identify Plasmodium vivax culture-adaptable strain.
text:
The lack of an in vitro culture system for Plasmodium vivax (Pv) has significantly impeded the progress of various
essential studies crucial for advancing our understanding and combating malaria. Leveraging our proximity to
infected patients in Cambodia, we propose (i) a systematic examination of various Pv clinical isolates to identify
culture-adaptable genotypes, (ii) a rigorous evaluation of culture conditions and (iii) to investigate the potential
role of mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) in Pv development. This comprehensive investigation will enhance our
understanding of Pv biology and facilitate the development of crucial tools for studying drug resistance and
devising anti-Plasmodium vivax strategies.

title: Mitigating Airborne PCB Emissions from Sediments with Black Carbon Materials and PCB-Degrading Biofilms
text:
PROJECT 5 – REMEDIATION IN SEDIMENTS
Project 5 of the Iowa Superfund Research Program will identify innovative strategies for optimizing performance
and extending the activity of PCB-degrading biofilm-coated black carbon materials in contaminated sediment
microcosms, determine important environmental factors and ecological interactions driving biofilm-mediated
airborne PCB bioremediation performance in mesocosm-scale reactors, and conduct a pilot-scale field
demonstration of biofilm-coated black carbon material bioaugmentation. We will demonstrate that the best
performing combinations of black carbon materials and microorganisms can effectively decrease airborne PCB
emissions from contaminated sediments and thus lessen human exposure to PCBs by inhalation in communities
located near Superfund sites. Therefore, the proposed research is pertinent to the goals of the Superfund
Research Program by developing advanced methods to reduce the amount and toxicity of PCBs in the
environment.

title: Decision support for ischemia imaging based on AI analysis of low-cost/no-cost screening CT and ECG data
text:
Using AI, we will utilize low-cost (arguably no additional cost) CT images and ECG data to identify patients at
risk for ischemia and create a physician decision-support tool for ordering advanced cardiac imaging. With low
actionable yields from advanced imaging, our decision-support tool will optimize resource use, reduce unneces-
sary tests, and ensure patients receive appropriate care.

title: Triggering Aberrant RNA Processing for RCC Therapy
text:
This proposal will investigate the mechanisms by which non-sense mediated decay (NMD) is upregulated in
clear cell kidney cancer as well as if triggering NMD can promote enhanced response to immune checkpoint
inhibition.

title: Project 4
text:
Project 4 NARRATIVE 
Project 4 will determine what cell-based human model systems best predict potential toxicity, 
including the extent of inter-individual and inter-tissue variability, in people who may be exposed to 
hazardous substances as a result of a disaster. We will also create a framework for testing mixtures 
of chemicals for toxicity in these cell-based systems and for how best to understand at what dose 
these mixtures may be harmful. The outcome of this project will be a set of experimental tools and 
computational models that can be used rapidly during/after natural or man-made disasters.

title: Novel Modulators of TGFß1 signaling in regulation of remyelination by neural stem cells
text:
Lack of remyelination results in axonal degeneration and debilitating clinical outcomes in demyelinating diseases
like Multiple Sclerosis. Here, we propose to determine how TGFβ1 signaling regulates remyelination through
Gpnmb, a novel modulator of the pathway, expressed highly in response to demyelination in neural stem cells.
These studies will help to determine new strategies for promoting remyelination in the diseased human brain.

title: Development of a high-throughput proteomic, transcriptomic, and metabolomic platform for multiomic profiling of same single-cells
text:
This proposal envisions the creation of a high-throughput single-cell multiomic platform capable of
simultaneously measuring proteins, transcripts, and metabolites. By advancing new chemical labeling, high-
density nanodroplet arrays, automated array handling, and integrated LC-MS workflows, the project will generate
unprecedented datasets linking transcriptional, translational, and metabolic regulation. These innovations will be
applied to peripheral blood mononuclear cells and pancreatic islet cells, enabling new insights into immune
activation and diabetes through systems-level analysis of amino acid signaling and biomolecular covariation.

title: Predicting neoadjuvant treatment response of locally advanced rectal cancer using co-registered endo-rectal photoacoustic and ultrasound imaging
text:
This study will advance and optimize a co-registered photoacoustic microscopy and ultrasound
endoscopic system to fill a critical gap in the current management of rectal cancer: identifying tumor
treatment response after neoadjuvant therapy. A clinical trial will evaluate the system’s ability to identify
treatment responders and therefore reduce morbidity in the treatment of this common disease. Finally,
serial surveillance of patients with complete responses to therapy will investigate markers of tumor
recurrence among this high risk population.

title: Mechanism-informed design of allosteric protein sensors
text:
Natural proteins function as “sensors” by binding ligands to shift their global conformational ensembles into new
functional states, but it remains challenging to design this behavior from first principles because we do not know
how each amino acid contributes to the energy of each state. We propose a new method to determine high-
resolution energetic information from hydrogen-deuterium exchange / mass spectrometry experiments to
investigate the evolution of natural protein sensors with the common Venus Flytrap (VFT) fold. We plan to apply
this knowledge to engineer artificial VFT-fold protein sensors for applications in sustainable plastic upcycling and
cell therapies to treat solid tumors.

title: Prognostic analysis and progression modeling of basal-like breast cancer using multi-region sequencing
text:
Basal cancer is a complex and deadly subtype of breast cancer. In this study, we will combine next-generation
sequencing technology and advanced computational methods to address some pressing issues and unmet
clinical needs of basal cancer, including those related to 1) the derivation of accurate prognostic evaluation
systems, 2) the delineation of the dynamic disease development process through progression modeling, and 3)
the identification of pivotal, driving molecular events that present therapeutic opportunities. If successfully
implemented, this study can significantly advance the basal cancer research, and pave the way for applying
similar strategies to study other deadly cancers.

title: In vivo and ex vivo gene editing for Artemis-deficient SCID
text:
Primary immune deficiencies are a rare group of inherited diseases caused by genetic
deficiency in patients who suffer from the inability to fight off common infections. In this grant
application we are working to repair the defective gene in the patients’ blood cells, thereby
restoring the ability of the patient to fight infections. The specific research proposed in this
application will first test the procedure by correcting the cells outside of the body, and then will
test a procedure for correcting the cells without having to remove them from the body.

title: Sex-specific Influences on tear microRNAs in dry eye disease
text:
Dry eye disease (DED) disproportionately affects females and displays variations among different racial
backgrounds. The purpose of this proposal is to investigate the sex- and race-specific disparities in tear
miRNAs and proteins, and their correlation with established DED subtypes and severity. Additionally, we will
establish a comprehensive database that compiles the miRNAs and proteins detected in human tear fluid,
providing a valuable resource to the scientific community.

title: Secondarily generalized tonic clonic seizure: a functional anatomy
text:
Frontal lobe epilepsy is the second most common form of epilepsy, and seizures associated with this
epilepsy are dangerous. We propose to map the neuronal circuits active during frontal lobe seizures
with unprecedented spatial and temporal resolution. These studies will open novel targets for therapy
by neuromodulation, resection, or drug treatment.

title: Identifying and Characterizing Firearm Storage Practices; Causal Links to Veteran Suicide
text:
Firearm suicide prevention is a leading VA priority. To date, firearm suicide preventions have almost entirely
focused on promoting in-home secure firearm storage to increase the time it would take for an individual with
suicidal intent to access a loaded firearm, but evidence to guide delivery of these interventions to the Veteran
population is lacking. The proposed effort will use innovative natural language processing methods to
characterize firearm storage practices (e.g., locked vs. unlocked) among Veterans. Data will then be merged
with templated data already available in the VA electronic health record to identify instances and describe
contexts in which Veterans have conflicting firearm data. Finally, the patient cohort will be linked to death
records to assess the associations between specific types of firearm storage practices and risk of firearm
suicide. These findings will provide important insights into specific storage methods that most protect Veterans
and Veteran subgroups, and will inform a variety of existing and future interventions.

title: Extracellular vesicle-dependent RNA signaling in metabolism
text: Successful completion of this pilot project will establish a framework for defining the functions and mechanisms of EV-dependent RNA transfer in metabolism and metabolic diseases. Furthermore, this work will facilitate the engineering of EV-based vehicles to selectively deliver therapeutics to target tissues for the treatment of these diseases.

title: Novel nanoparticles to stimulate therapeutic angiogenesis in peripheral arterial disease
text:
Peripheral arterial disease (PAD), an illness commonly found in the elderly and caused by arterial occlusion in
the lower body, affects more than 200 million people worldwide and is associated with high rates of morbidity
and mortality. To reduce these complications and improve the quality of life for PAD patients, our research aims
to develop novel biodegradable nanoparticles to deliver therapeutic agents that specifically protect cells under
ischemic stress conditions, facilitate the formation of blood vessels under hypoxia, and facilitate noninvasive
multimodal imaging methods, such as fluorescent and photoacoustic imaging, to monitor the progress of this
therapeutic intervention. The impact of our research is significant as these new nanoparticle platforms could be
used to deliver any therapeutics locally, treat this disease effectively, and monitor the treatment noninvasively
by imaging.

title: Investigating the role of CHASERR in CHD2 regulation, chromatin architecture, and gene expression during neurodevelopment
text:
It has been known that reduced production of chromatin remodeler CHD2 causes a severe pediatric
neurological disorder. Recent evidence suggests that deletion of CHASERR, a long non-coding RNA upstream
of CHD2, leads to too much CHD2 production and disease, yet the precise mechanism of how CHASERR
regulates CHD2 expression is not known. This training proposal aims to leverage cellular models, including
patient-specific stem cells, and multi-omics approaches to determine the mechanism of cis-regulation of CHD2
by CHASERR, and how too much CHD2 leads to global changes in chromatin architecture and gene
expression in neurodevelopment.
